# Gap analysis: `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md`

This spec has no Synthesize-mode header, so I entered through your explicit request to compare it against the code. No roadmap exists under `specs/`, and there is no `specs/deferred_items.md`. The repo holds only `uv init` scaffolds, so every requirement is `missing`. I have not written any roadmap text yet. A few questions below change how the work is partitioned, so they come first.

| Req | Verdict | Evidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Baseline | missing | none found. I searched `packages/*/src`, the root, and checked for `tests/` | Only `hello()` stubs exist |
| R2 Continuation | missing | none found (same search) | |
| R3 Processing | missing | none found (same search) | |
| R4 Platform | missing | none found. No `infra/` or `conf/` | §4.9 puts the infrastructure in this repo (`infra/azure/…`), so this is `missing`, not `out-of-repo` |
| R5 Shared implementation | missing | none found | |

| (none) | in-code-but-not-in-spec | `packages/sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest` | §4.9 names only `sec-edgar-ingest`. The spec says "no repository was supplied" (header, §8), so it never saw these three packages |
| (none) | in-code-but-not-in-spec | root `pyproject.toml`: `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` | The script points at a module that doesn't exist |

This will not be a single-stage exit. The work spans the worker, manifest/publication, reconciliation, infrastructure and live operation (§7 Phase 1 and Phase 2), which is several spec→plan cycles.

## Questions

1. **Package layout.** §4.9 puts all of the code into `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repo also has `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, which suggests a split you already had in mind. What should each one hold?
   - *My default:* `sec-edgar-client` holds the shared, throttled, lease-holding SEC downloader (R8, §4.3), so later consumers can't bypass the request budget. `sec-edgar-index-ingest` holds this spec's ETL and CLI. `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-ingest` stay untouched, since filing documents and JSON are out of scope (§2.2).
   - Whatever you choose, the §4.9 paths and CLI name change, so I'd fold the answer back into the spec. If the boundary is contested, it's worth an ADR.
2. **Acceptance.** The spec and ADR are both PROPOSED, and §7.1 starts with accepting them. Should I partition now, with Stage 1 gated on acceptance, or wait until you've accepted them?
   - *My default:* partition now and gate Stage 1.
3. **Root `sec-edgar` script.** Should I remove it, or do you intend a top-level CLI? If you intend one, it isn't in the spec.
4. **Backfill range.** §4.6 says golden fixtures must cover every historical index format in the chosen range before that range is supported. Do you know `backfill.start_quarter` yet?
   - This decides whether a cheap investigation stage (a format survey) goes first and how wide it is.
   - *My default if you don't know:* the survey covers the whole archive, and the result informs the choice of range.
5. **Spec freshness.** The spec says no repo was inspected (header, §8). Should I record the real repo state in the spec as part of answering Q1, or leave the spec as it is and keep the mapping only in the roadmap?
   - *My default:* amend the spec, so writing-plans has one source of truth.

Once you answer, I'll write `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md` and bring you the stage partition for approval before Stage 1.
